title: buildSrc, Included Builds, and Build-Logic Boundaries Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies buildsrc, included builds, and build-logic boundaries?
options: Select an isolated build-logic boundary and expose stable plugins rather than script-time mutation helpers.
Depend build logic on app modules
Use an included build without verification review
questions.answer: Select an isolated build-logic boundary and expose stable plugins rather than script-time mutation helpers.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: An included build and buildSrc have identical isolation and invalidation behaviour.
questions.explanation: Moving copied scripts into buildSrc without extracting plugins still leaves imperative helpers, hidden mutation and little functional-test surface.

questions.prompt: What is the main architectural benefit of a build-logic included build?
questions.answer: It provides an explicit, separately structured and testable build boundary with stable plugin interfaces.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
